subject: AuroraPay portal onboarding — presign/KMS scope clarification
messages:
From: Marie Lam <marie.lam@aurorapay.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aurorapay.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor portal onboarding + S3 presign guidance request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Procurement and security here at AuroraPay are ready to move forward with the vendor portal onboarding (we prefer Vendr but can accept Whistic if needed). Before we kick off, the security team asked for a few clarifications so we can scope the evidence upload window correctly: 

- Do you support pre-signed S3 uploads for evidence ingestion, or do you require us to transfer artifacts through your secure uploader?
- If presign is supported, what are the required object key formats and any required metadata/hash manifest we should include?
- We're subject to a KMS policy that rotates monthly; will that affect signed artifact verification on your end?
- For SOC 2 artifacts we need to keep a clear chain of custody — do you accept golden-checksum manifests and a CAIQ/SIG mapping spreadsheet?

We want to avoid repeated manual uploads. If you can share a short preflight checklist (permissions, bucket policy, IAM role, TTL on presigned URLs) that would be great. I attached a high-level onboarding timeline from procurement.

Can you loop in the engineer who owns presign integration? We hope to have the first evidence batch in the week of June 14.

Thanks,

Marie Lam
Sr. Procurement Manager
AuroraPay
attachments: Aurora_Onboarding_Timeline_v3.pdf (pdf, 215KB)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marie Lam <marie.lam@aurorapay.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor portal onboarding + S3 presign guidance request

Hi Marie — thanks for the detailed note and the timeline. Looping in Laura (security operations) and Ben (platform integrations) to confirm technical specifics. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, Vendr + our portal ingestion flow supports pre-signed S3 uploads. We also maintain a secure uploader if customers prefer direct web upload.
- Required presign pattern: s3://redwood-evidence/<customer-id>/<year>-<month>/<artifact-type>/<filename>. We ask that each presigned object include metadata: x-amz-meta-artifact-type (soc2|sig|caiq), x-amz-meta-evidence-id (UUID) and sha256 checksum in the x-amz-meta-sha256 header.
- KMS rotation is fine as long as the presign is generated by an IAM role that remains valid. We verify the checksum after download and record the object ETag and a digest in the audit trail — rotations don't invalidate existing presigned URLs but do change who can generate them.
- CAIQ/SIG mapping spreadsheet is exactly the kind of artifact we prefer for mapping controls to uploaded evidence. Provide a single CSV or XLSX and include a manifest JSON that points to presign keys and checksums.

Action items I propose:
1) Laura and Ben will add a short preflight checklist and a one-page presign example.
2) We will send a small test presign for a 3MB proof artifact so you can validate the flow before the bulk upload.
3) Agree a retention TTL for the staging bucket (we usually request 14 days for verification, but can be adjusted).

Laura/Ben — can you draft the checklist and the presign example by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Vendor portal onboarding + S3 presign guidance request

On Wed, Jun 2, 2027 at 10:01 AM karthik.iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Quick answers up front:
> - Yes, Vendr + our portal ingestion flow supports pre-signed S3 uploads.
> - Required presign pattern: s3://redwood-evidence/<customer-id>/<year>-<month>/<artifact-type>/<filename>.

Hi all — adding the checklist and technical notes below so Aurora's infra team has exactly what they need. Ben and I validated this against our ingestion pipeline this morning.

Presign preflight checklist (short):
- IAM role: create role AuroraPresignUploader with sts:AssumeRole trust for your pipeline account. Attach policy allowing PutObject, PutObjectAcl, and GetObject for the target prefix.
- Bucket policy: allow PutObject for the IAM role and deny public ACLs. Example condition: "aws:SecureTransport": "true"
- Object metadata: include x-amz-meta-artifact-type, x-amz-meta-evidence-id, x-amz-meta-sha256. Keep evidence-id stable for related bundles.
- TTL: default 14 days. If you need <14, confirm so we can run verification earlier.
- Manifest: one manifest.csv at the root of the upload folder listing filename, presigned-url (for our verification only), sha256, control-mapping (SIG/CAIQ control id), and date-uploaded.
- KMS: presigned urls generated by the uploader role are acceptable; ensure kms:Encrypt permissions for generation if you use AWS KMS with encryption. Rotation: schedule is fine — we record object-level checksum and ETag at ingest.

Minimal presign example (short):
- Prefix: s3://redwood-evidence/aurorapay/2027-06/soc2/Aurora-SSO-KB-2026.pdf
- Metadata headers:
  x-amz-meta-artifact-type: soc2
  x-amz-meta-evidence-id: 3f47b8c2-9a1e-4da8-8c3b-0a2f7f9e5e21
  x-amz-meta-sha256: 5e884898da28047151d0e56f8dc6292773603d0d

Attachments (for Aurora):
- Aurorapay-presign-policy-example.json (json, 3KB); redwood-presign-instructions.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

Ben — can you post the sample presign generator payload to the shared Drive link and I'll confirm the bucket policy snippet?

Laura Bennett
Security Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
